Repository: re-cinq/HALEngine
Ticket: #144 Deliver a user's conversation list over the WebSocket protocol

The pull request for this ticket has a RED build. Your job is to make it
green, on the branch you are already on, and nothing else.

The ticket's branch is checked out with write access at /var/tmp/loop-bench/runs/8c1337efa4b5/workspace/target.
Run every command from inside it (`cd /var/tmp/loop-bench/runs/8c1337efa4b5/workspace/target` first). The ticket
is at `/var/tmp/loop-bench/runs/8c1337efa4b5/workspace/ticket.md`: read it before anything else. Pass `repo` (the
owner/name your task names above) on every `lore_*` call: the gateway has
no checkout to detect it from.

CI is the judge of this branch, and the `CI reported failures` section
of `/var/tmp/loop-bench/runs/8c1337efa4b5/workspace/round-brief.md` is its verdict: the sha it judged, the checks that failed, and for
each — when CI published them — the annotations (`path:line message`),
the step that failed, and what it printed. Start from it, not from a
full local build.

WHEN THE VERDICT NAMES A FILE AND LINE — an annotation such as
`specs/x/spec.md:7 Status "draft" does not match ...` — open that file
at that line and fix what it says. Do not install dependencies, build
the workspace, or run the suite to confirm a finding CI already made
about a specific line; a lint or status error on a markdown file needs
an editor, not `npm ci`. Run a command only when the FIX needs one: a
test you must see fail, a typecheck of a package whose code you changed.
When that command's toolchain is not in this pod (`java`, `mvn`,
`gradle`, `go`, `cargo` or `dotnet` is not found), do not look for it and
do not install it: fix from the verdict, push, and let CI judge the push.

When it names the failed STEP and what that step printed but no
annotation, that is the diagnosis: find that step in
`.github/workflows/` and run only that step's command. When it names
only a check, map the check name to the job that publishes it, find the
command that job runs, and run ONLY that. Reproducing the whole build to
rediscover what you have already been told costs the ticket a pod and
tells you nothing new. The pod's Bash hook refuses a test runner given
no path, no workspace flag and no `cd` into the step's directory, so a
repo-wide `vitest run` never starts.

RUN A STEP'S COMMAND WHERE CI RAN IT, never from wherever your shell
happens to be. When the report says `Ran as: npm script <script> of
package <package>` (`npm_script` in `lore_get_ci_failures`), run
`npm run <script> -w <package>` from the repository root — or plain
`npm run <script>` if <package> is the root package.json's own name.
For any other step, take the directory from the workflow step itself
(its `working-directory:`, a `cd`, or a `-w`/`--prefix` in its `run:`).
A package's test command run at the repo root is NOT that command:
`npx vitest run` there discovers every package's suite. Run 754cb4fa ran
nine suites with coverage for 43 minutes and hit its deadline answering
what one package's suite answers in minutes.

NEVER RUN THE LINTER IN THIS POD, scoped or not. CI ran it on a machine
sized for it; here a two-file `eslint` peaks near 800 MB against a 1Gi
pod, and runs 112256d9 and 62c1ca5e were OOM-killed on it. When the red
check is a lint or format job, its findings are what you fix, not what
you reproduce: take the file and line from the annotation, or ask CI
with `lore_get_ci_failures` and then `lore_get_ci_job_log` with
`grep: "error"`. Format only the files this branch changed
(`git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD`); typecheck nothing here —
CI's build step already did, and it does not fit this pod.

IF THE SECTION IS MISSING OR TOO THIN, ASK CI YOURSELF: call
`lore_get_ci_failures` with `repo` (owner/name) and `branch` (the output
of `git branch --show-current`) — it reports on that branch: the judged
sha, the conclusion, and each failed check with its annotations, failed
steps and log tail. When a failure needs more of its log, call
`lore_get_ci_job_log` with `repo` and that failure's `job_id`, a `grep`
for the report's error marker (`error`, `FAIL`, `✖`) and a small `tail`.
Never reinstall or rebuild the workspace to learn what CI already
printed.

FIRST, check the branch has not moved since CI judged it. The section's
heading names the sha CI read (`judged_sha` from `lore_get_ci_failures`
when the section is absent); run `git log --format=%s <that sha>..HEAD`.
If any commit it lists does not carry `[skip ci]`,
the branch moved after CI judged it: somebody pushed, and CI has not
judged the new head yet.
Change nothing and run nothing, and end with
LORE_NODE_RESULT: {"outcome":"success","extras":{"ci_fixed":"branch moved past <sha>; CI re-judges the head"}}
The wait re-reads CI on the new head and sends the branch back here only
if that is red too.

BEFORE YOU READ ANY FILE, ask the graph what has failed here before.
For every path the red output names, call `lore-query-trace` with
`failures_touching` set to that path. Each row is a previous failed
attempt on that file: what failed, on which commit, and — when a later
attempt fixed it — the sha that did. `git show` that sha. This repo has
very likely hit this exact error before, and the diff that ended it last
time is the cheapest thing you will read today.

A row that says `still open` was never fixed; treat it as a warning that
the obvious fix did not work before, not as a solution to copy.

RULES:
- Fix EVERY finding the verdict names, in this visit, in the order
  listed. There is no local re-run here that would reveal the rest, and
  each finding you leave costs the ticket a round: run 2a291314's repair
  fixed one of three and the build came back red twice more. Do not add
  speculative fixes for failures the verdict did not name.
- Fix the cause, not the symptom. Never delete, skip, `.only`, `.todo` or
  loosen a test to go green; never widen a type to `any` to silence a
  typecheck error; never add an eslint-disable to pass lint. If the test
  is genuinely wrong, say why in your final message before you change it.
- Change only what the red build requires. Unrelated edits make the
  re-review harder and are not what was asked.
- If the named check's command passes locally, say exactly what you ran
  and what passed — the failure may be environment-only, and that is a
  finding, not a fix.

DELIVERY, NON-NEGOTIABLE — the next step runs in a DIFFERENT container:
- Before you commit, run the repository's FORMATTER over the files you
  changed (`npx prettier --write <files>`, `gofmt -w <files>`, whichever
  this repo uses) and nothing else from CI's checklist. Do NOT run the
  linter in this pod: CI runs it on every push, and here it does not
  fit — in this repository a two-file `eslint` peaks near 800 MB against
  a 1Gi pod, and runs 112256d9 and 62c1ca5e were OOM-killed on exactly
  that. A lint finding comes back as a red build naming the file and
  line, which the next round fixes with an editor.
- Do NOT typecheck here either. A green test is not a compiled build —
  vitest transpiles each file without checking types — but CI's build
  step is what proves it, and in this repository `tsc --noEmit` on
  `libs/shared` peaks near 950 MB against the 1Gi pod: run 2a291314's
  dod pod was OOM-killed on it. A type error comes back as a red build
  whose failed step and log tail name the file and line; the next
  round fixes it there. Read your imports and signatures twice instead.
- NEVER run a workspace build in this pod (`npm run build`, `tsc -b`, a
  `tsc` without `--noEmit`): tests resolve every workspace package from
  SOURCE, so nothing needs building for a test to see your change, and
  the build is the 950 MB step that OOM-killed run abac6ee9 while it
  rebuilt libs/shared for a test that never needed it.
- When the work is done, `git -C /var/tmp/loop-bench/runs/8c1337efa4b5/workspace/target add` what you changed and commit it with a
  short, factual message. Then `git -C /var/tmp/loop-bench/runs/8c1337efa4b5/workspace/target push origin HEAD`. The clone carries
  its own credentials, so a plain push authenticates; you need no token
  and must never look for one.
- Then bring the branch up to date with its base — `git fetch origin main`
  and merge `origin/main` in — and push again if that produced anything.
  A branch that cannot merge cleanly gets NO CI AT ALL: GitHub runs no
  workflow on a conflicted pull request, so the ticket parks on a build
  that will never start. Resolve any conflict now, favouring `origin/main`
  for anything this ticket did not write, and never by discarding your own
  work. This is why a nine-day-old branch stalled: 186 commits of drift,
  no checks, and a wait with nothing to wait for.
- Confirm it landed: `git status` must report the branch is not ahead of
  its upstream. An unpushed commit lives only in this container and
  dies with it — do NOT report success for one.
- If you changed nothing because the branch moved, end as the FIRST check
  above says. If you changed nothing for any other reason, say why and
  report `changes_requested` below, never `failed`: a failed repair ends
  the ticket, and the branch may already be green.
- Do not open a pull request: you have no `gh` and no GitHub token. Lore
  opens the PR from the branch you push.

Print exactly one of these as the last line of your final message:
- You reproduced a failure, fixed it, and the build passes locally:
  LORE_NODE_RESULT: {"outcome":"success","extras":{"ci_fixed":"<one line: what was broken>"}}
- You could not make it green, or the failure is not in this repository:
  LORE_NODE_RESULT: {"outcome":"changes_requested","extras":{"ci_blocked":"<one line: what you ran and what stayed red>"}}

commit 2926558eb8287942fc3ff3636da112e8eee3d2bd
Author: vvondruska <2923801+vvondruska@users.noreply.github.com>
Date:   Tue Oct 6 13:42:56 2026 +0200

    feat(session): list a user's conversations from the store (#146)
    
    * feat(session): list a user's conversations from the store
    
    Resume rejoins one conversation - the id a client names, or the user's
    latest - and no store member could say which conversations exist, so a
    consumer wanting a conversation list had to query the collection behind
    the engine's back.
    
    Adds the optional `SessionStore.listFor(userId, options?)`, answering
    `SessionSummary` rows (sessionId, createdAt, updatedAt, entryCount) most
    recent activity first, with `limit` (50 default, 200 cap) and `before`
    paging. A summary carries neither entries nor credentials.
    
    InMemorySessionStore reads the activity `latestFor` already computes, so
    a list's first row is always the session a resume would rejoin. Mongo
    filters on the user in the query, sorts on the index `latestFor` needs
    and projects the entries away; `save` now writes an `entryCount` field
    so a list counts a conversation without reading one.
    
    Refs #143
    Relates to re-cinq/Otto#313
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
    
    * fix(session): page a conversation list on a total order
    
    Paging on `updatedAt` alone dropped a conversation whenever two of a
    user's shared an activity time and the page boundary fell between them:
    three sessions created in the same millisecond listed the first page and
    then answered nothing, so two conversations were unreachable.
    
    `SessionListOptions.before` is now a `SessionCursor` of `updatedAt` and
    `sessionId` - the last summary the caller saw satisfies it - and both
    stores order on that pair, so a tie cannot straddle a boundary. Mongo
    sorts `{updatedAt: -1, _id: -1}` and filters the tie with `$or`.
    
    A limit of 0 now answers nothing rather than one row. Mongo is never
    asked for it: the driver reads `limit: 0` as no limit at all and would
    have answered with every conversation the filter matched. A limit that
    is not a usable number reads as none given.
    
    In-memory `listFor` and `latestFor` now break a tie differently - id
    against creation order - which the spec and docs state.
    
    Refs #143
    
    * fix(session): make a conversation cursor and its index hold up
    
    An independent review found three defects and an undeclared break.
    
    A cursor whose updatedAt had been through JSON - which is how any real
    client pages - threw a TypeError in memory and silently matched nothing
    on mongo, so a client read a truncated history as the end of it.
    SessionCursor.updatedAt now takes a Date, an ISO string or an epoch
    number, and one carrying no usable moment is refused by name rather than
    read as no cursor at all.
    
    listFor sorts on two keys, which the documented {userId, updatedAt}
    index cannot satisfy: mongo answered a 50-row page by sorting all 300
    of a user's conversations, so paging a long history was quadratic and a
    large one could exceed the 100MB sort limit outright. The index to
    create is now three keys, and a test pins that the two-key form sorts
    where the three-key form does not.
    
    MongoSessionStore.latestFor had no tie-break, so on equal updatedAt it
    answered the opposite end of the tie from listFor while the spec claimed
    they agreed. It now breaks the tie by _id.
    
    CollectionLike is exported, so the required `find` this branch added
    broke any consumer's hand-written adapter. It is optional now, listFor
    refuses a collection without it rather than reporting an empty history,
    and CursorLike, FindManyOptions and FindOneOptions are exported for
    anyone implementing one.
    
    Refs #143
    
    * test(session): pin that both stores answer one conversation list
    
    Closes the review's remaining gaps. A new suite drives the in-memory and
    mongo stores through the same conversations and asserts they answer one
    order - activity apart and tied - and page identically through the
    documented `{limit, before: rows.at(-1)}` call, which no test exercised
    with a limit above one. Writing it caught a bug in itself first: both
    scenarios shared one collection, so the second run's upserts overwrote
    the first's.
    
    The summary-shape test asserted undefined on an object literal it had
    built, which proved nothing. It now reads a real summary out of a store
    created with credentials and pins its exact key set, so a later change
    that let an entry or a header into the row fails here.
    
    A negative limit no longer answers an empty list. It reads as no limit
    given, like a non-finite one, since an empty history for a typo is the
    worse reading; only an explicit 0 answers nothing.
    
    Also: the spec status takes the canonical `Shipped`, and the changelog
    no longer implies the engine serves the list - the store answers it and
    the consumer still writes the route.
    
    Refs #143
    
    * docs(session): say how to tell a conversation list has more pages
    
    listFor answers an array and no hasMore, which left a consumer to invent
    the pattern or, worse, to reach for count(). The listing section now
    documents the short-page and over-fetch readings, including that the 200
    cap tops the over-fetch out at a page of 199.
    
    The count() note said what it counts but never whose: every user's, not
    one user's, so putting it in front of a user both misreports their
    history and discloses the size of everyone else's. A per-user count is
    re-cinq/HALEngine#147.
    
    Refs #143
    
    * docs(session): measure the list query as the store actually issues it
    
    The claim that the three-key index made a page a covered query came from
    a probe projecting only _id. The store projects createdAt and entryCount
    too, neither of which is in the index, so mongo still fetches every row
    it answers with: a 50-row page examines 50, not none. The two-key figure
    stands - it examines all 300.
    
    The point survives the correction and is now stated as what it is: with
    the index the work is the page, without it the work is the history.
    
    The index test now issues the store's own projection and asserts both
    examined counts beside the sort distinction, so the figures in the docs
    cannot drift from what mongo does again.
    
    Refs #143
    
    ---------
    
    Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

parameters.new_string:
## Done when these pass

- [x] **listing conversations over the WebSocket protocol › answers list_sessions for the authenticated user with ISO dates, forwarding limit and before while ignoring any client userId** — Sends `{type: 'list_sessions', limit, before, userId}` over a connected WebSocket and verifies `store.listFor` is called with the socket's authenticated `userId` (`session.userId`) and `{limit, before}`, answering `{type: 'session_list', sessions}` with `createdAt` and `updatedAt` serialised as ISO-8601 strings.
  `src/transport/conversationList.acceptance.test.ts`

- [x] **listing conversations over the WebSocket protocol › answers an empty session_list when the store has no listFor, and SERVER_ERROR with a ws error log when listFor throws** — Verifies that a store without `listFor` answers `{type: 'session_list', sessions: []}` and a store whose `listFor` throws/rejects logs an error under category `'ws'` with the userId and error message and answers `{type: 'error', code: 'SERVER_ERROR'}`.
  `src/transport/conversationList.acceptance.test.ts`

- [x] **listing conversations over the WebSocket protocol › accepts a bare list_sessions frame and rejects a malformed limit or before with INVALID_MESSAGE without calling listFor** — Verifies that `{type: 'list_sessions'}` is accepted while non-integer or negative `limit` values and malformed `before` cursors (`sessionId` outside 1–128 chars or unparseable `updatedAt`) are rejected with `INVALID_MESSAGE` without invoking `store.listFor`.
  `src/transport/conversationList.acceptance.test.ts`

## Facets

- [x] Add `ListSessionsMessage`, `SessionSummaryFrame`, and `SessionListMessage` to `src/types/messages.ts`, include them in `IncomingMessage` and `OutgoingMessage`, and re-export them from `src/index.ts`.
- [x] Validate `list_sessions` frames in `src/transport/ws/validation.ts` (optional non-negative integer `limit`; optional `before` object with 1–128 char `sessionId` and finite-date `updatedAt` string or number; strip unknown fields like `userId`).
- [x] Thread `sessionStore` into `createMessageHandler` (optional parameter so existing 1-arg and 2-arg callers keep working) and wire it in `src/transport/createServer.ts`.
- [x] Handle `list_sessions` in `src/transport/ws/messageHandler.ts` (and helper in `src/transport/ws/sender.ts` if needed) by reading `session.userId`, calling `await sessionStore?.listFor?.(session.userId, {limit, before})`, serialising `Date` fields to ISO strings, and on error logging via `log.error('ws', ...)` and sending `ErrorCodes.SERVER_ERROR`.
- [x] Document `list_sessions` and `session_list` in `specs/hal-engine-websocket-protocol/spec.md` and `specs/hal-engine-conversation-list/spec.md`.
